questions.stem:
Two agents can each trigger the workflow that deploys `orders-api` to production. Requirements:

- The operations team must approve every production deployment.
- Only one deployment can run at a time.
- A deployment that has started must never be interrupted.

The repository has an environment named `production` with the operations team as required reviewers. How should you complete the deploy job? Select the correct option for each box.
questions.template:
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: [[env]]
    concurrency:
      group: [[group]]
      cancel-in-progress: [[cancel]]
    steps:
      - run: ./deploy.sh

env.rationale: Only the exact name `production` picks up the required reviewers. Any other name creates a new environment with no protection rules.

group.rationale: A fixed group name is shared by every run, so they're serialised. `run_id` and `sha` give each run (or commit) its own group, so nothing waits.

cancel.rationale: `false` lets the running deployment finish while the next one waits. `true` would cancel a deployment mid-way.

questions.explanation: The environment provides the human gate, and a shared concurrency group with `cancel-in-progress: false` serialises deployments without interrupting one that has started.
questions.takeaway: Exact environment name for the gate; shared group + cancel-in-progress: false to serialise safely.

questions.scenario:
A workflow in `contoso/orders-api` runs an agent step that authenticates with `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The workflow declares `permissions: contents: write` and `actions: write`.

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

items.statement: When the agent pushes a commit to a branch of `contoso/orders-api` with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, workflows in that repository that run `on: push` are triggered.
items.explanation: Events created with `GITHUB_TOKEN` don't start new workflow runs, to prevent recursive loops.

items.statement: The agent can start another workflow in `contoso/orders-api` by sending a `workflow_dispatch` event with `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
items.explanation: `workflow_dispatch` and `repository_dispatch` are the exceptions: they do start runs when sent with `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Dispatching a workflow needs `actions: write`.

items.statement: The agent can push a commit to `contoso/shared-libs`, another repository in the same organisation, with the same `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
items.explanation: `GITHUB_TOKEN` is scoped to the repository that runs the workflow. Cross-repository writes need a GitHub App token (or, less ideally, a personal token).

questions.takeaway: GITHUB_TOKEN: one repository, one job, and its events don't trigger new runs except dispatch events.

questions.stem:
Over the last month, most pull requests from your Copilot custom agent fail the same lint rule (`IDE0055`, formatting). Reviewers keep sending them back, which slows delivery. You want to reduce how often it happens and make sure non-compliant code can never be merged.

Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Add the formatting convention and the command `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` to the agent's instructions so it runs the check before finishing.
options.rationale: Correct. This tunes the agent's behaviour at the instructions layer so the error happens less often. On its own it's guidance, which is why you also need an enforced check.

options.text: Make the lint job a required status check in the ruleset for `main`.
options.rationale: Correct. A required check is the enforced gate: a pull request that fails formatting can't be merged, whatever the agent claims.

options.text: Switch the agent to a larger model.
options.rationale: Incorrect. It might reduce the error rate, but it isn't targeted at the root cause and it enforces nothing.

options.text: Disable `IDE0055` in `.editorconfig` for files changed by the agent.
options.rationale: Incorrect. It hides the signal instead of fixing the behaviour and lowers the quality bar.

options.text: Add the agent to the ruleset bypass list so formatting issues don't block it.
options.rationale: Incorrect. The bypass list lets an actor skip every rule. Never put an agent on it.

questions.explanation: Fix recurring agent failures at two layers: tune the instructions so the error happens less, and enforce the standard with a required check so it can't be merged when it does happen.
questions.takeaway: Recurring agent error → tune instructions (prevent) + required check (enforce). Never hide the signal or bypass the gate.
